figures.caption: Figure 2: The height of each bar corresponds to the estimated mean squared error (MSE) of an estimator from the simulation study of Section 5.1, based on 1000 simulations. Each panel corresponds to a different value of the parameter θ, which quantifies the degree of covariate shift between the experimental and observational datasets. The estimators τ̂aipsw and τ̂collab are compared to the true transported average treatment effect τ while the estimator ˆ̄τ is compared to the projected treatment effect τ̄ . The shaded part of each bar corresponds to the estimated variance while the unshaded part of each bar corresponds to the estimated squared bias.

Figure 1: A map from Fig. 1 of Kluger et al. (2022) showing the 11 locations with available data from crop rotation field experiments (letters), along with colored dots showing the locations and average number of extreme degree days (EDD) of extensive satellite observations spanning the region of interest.
Figure 4: Same as Fig. 2, but for the multivariate covariate simulations in Section 5.2
Figure 3: For each value of θ studied in the simulations from Section 5.1, a plot of the weight function w(·) in (4) with γ given by (22).

Figure 5: Histograms of the three estimators across the 100 simulations from the crop rotation dataset described in Section 5.3. The black vertical dashed lines show the values of the true estimand — the transported ATE τ ≈ 0.905 for the estimators τ̂aipsw and τ̂collab, and the projected ATE τ̄ ≈ 0.906 for the estimator ˆ̄τ .
Table 1: The empirical coverage probabilities (left) and mean widths (right) for the nominal 95% confidence intervals considered in the simulation study of Section 5.1, across 1000 simulations.
